name: Logic & Riddles
description: Sequences, odd-ones-out, syllogisms, riddles and brain-bending word problems.
question: {prompt}

cards.prompt: What comes next? 2, 4, 6, 8, …
cards.fact: Each term adds 2: the even numbers.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, …
cards.fact: These are the square numbers: 1², 2², 3², 4², 5², so next is 6² = 36.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …
cards.fact: Fibonacci: each number is the sum of the two before it (5 + 8 = 13).

cards.prompt: What comes next? 3, 9, 27, 81, …
cards.fact: Each term is multiplied by 3: 81 × 3 = 243.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …
cards.fact: These are the prime numbers; 13 is the next one after 11.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, …
cards.fact: The gaps grow by one each time: +1, +2, +3, +4, then +5.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 1, 8, 27, 64, …
cards.fact: These are cubes: 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, so next is 5³ = 125.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, …
cards.fact: Triangular numbers: add 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6.

cards.prompt: What comes next? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, …

cards.fact: The digits are in alphabetical order: eight, five, four, nine, one, seven, six, three, two, zero.
Read each term aloud: 111221 is "three 1s, two 2s, one 1" → 312211.

cards.prompt: What comes next? A, C, E, G, …
cards.fact: Every other letter of the alphabet: skip one each time.

cards.prompt: What comes next? M, T, W, T, F, S, …
cards.fact: Days of the week: Monday through Saturday, then Sunday.

cards.prompt: What comes next? Z, X, V, T, …
cards.fact: Going backwards through the alphabet, skipping one letter each time.

cards.prompt: What comes next? B, E, H, K, …
cards.fact: Each letter jumps 3 places forward: B(2), E(5), H(8), K(11), N(14).

cards.prompt: What comes next? J, F, M, A, M, J, J, …
cards.fact: First letters of the months: January to July, then August.

cards.prompt: What comes next? A, B, D, G, K, …
cards.fact: The gaps grow: +1, +2, +3, +4, then +5 takes K (11) to P (16).

cards.prompt: What comes next? O, T, T, F, F, S, S, E, …
cards.fact: First letters of One, Two, Three… Eight, so next is Nine.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: apple, banana, carrot, cherry?
cards.fact: A carrot is a root vegetable; the others are fruits.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: whale, dolphin, shark, seal?
cards.fact: Sharks are fish; whales, dolphins and seals are mammals that breathe air.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: Paris, Berlin, Sydney, Madrid, Rome?
cards.fact: Sydney isn't a national capital (Australia's is Canberra); the others are.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon?
cards.fact: The Moon is a natural satellite; the others are planets.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: pentagon, hexagon, octagon, sphere?
cards.fact: A sphere is a 3D solid; the others are flat polygons.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: violin, cello, flute, harp?
cards.fact: The flute is a wind instrument; the others are string instruments.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13?
cards.fact: 9 = 3 × 3, so it is not prime; all the others are prime numbers.

cards.prompt: Which is the odd one out: knee, elbow, wrist, femur?
cards.fact: The femur is a bone (the thigh bone); the others are joints.

cards.prompt: All bloops are razzies. All razzies are lazzies. Are all bloops definitely lazzies?
cards.fact: If A is inside B and B is inside C, then A must be inside C.

cards.prompt: Tom is taller than Ann. Ann is taller than Raj. Who is the shortest?
cards.fact: Order them: Tom > Ann > Raj, so Raj is shortest.

cards.prompt: No fish are dogs. All goldfish are fish. Can a goldfish be a dog?
cards.fact: Every goldfish is a fish, and no fish is a dog, so no goldfish is a dog.

cards.prompt: All cats are mammals. Some mammals are black. Must some cats be black?
cards.fact: The black mammals might all be non-cats, such as black bears, so nothing follows about cats.

cards.prompt: Mia is older than Leo but younger than Zoe. Zoe is younger than Kai. Who is the second oldest?
cards.fact: From oldest to youngest: Kai, Zoe, Mia, Leo.

cards.prompt: If it rains, the grass gets wet. The grass is wet. Did it definitely rain?
cards.fact: That's the fallacy of affirming the consequent: a sprinkler could have wet the grass.

cards.prompt: What has keys but can't open locks?
cards.fact: A piano has 88 keys, but not one of them opens a door.

cards.prompt: What has hands but can't clap?
cards.fact: A clock's hands point at the time but can never applaud.

cards.prompt: What gets wetter the more it dries?
cards.fact: A towel soaks up water as it dries you off.

cards.prompt: What has a neck but no head?
cards.fact: A bottle's narrow top is called its neck.

cards.prompt: I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old. What am I?
cards.fact: A candle burns down shorter as it ages.

cards.prompt: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
cards.fact: Every step you take leaves a footprint behind you.

cards.prompt: A rooster lays an egg on the peak of a barn roof. Which way does it roll?
cards.fact: Roosters are male chickens, and they don't lay eggs.

cards.prompt: How many months of the year have 28 days?
cards.fact: Every month has at least 28 days; February just stops there (most years).

cards.prompt: A farmer has 17 sheep. All but 9 run away. How many are left?
cards.fact: "All but 9" means 9 stayed behind.

cards.prompt: In a race, you overtake the person in second place. What place are you in now?
cards.fact: You took second place from them; the leader is still ahead of you.

cards.prompt: A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How many cents does the ball cost?
cards.fact: Ball = 5¢, bat = $1.05; together $1.10. Most people blurt out 10¢.

cards.prompt: 5 machines take 5 minutes to make 5 widgets. How many minutes would 100 machines take to make 100 widgets?
cards.fact: Each machine makes one widget in 5 minutes, so 100 machines make 100 widgets in 5 minutes.

cards.prompt: A patch of lily pads doubles in size every day. It covers the whole lake on day 48. On what day was half the lake covered?
cards.fact: It doubles daily, so the day before it was full it was half full.

cards.prompt: You have 3 pills and must take one every half hour, starting now. How many minutes until all are taken?
cards.fact: Take them at 0, 30 and 60 minutes, so it takes just one hour.

cards.prompt: 2 people dig 2 holes in 2 hours. At the same rate, how many holes can 4 people dig in 4 hours?
cards.fact: Each person digs 1 hole per 2 hours, so 4 people × 2 holes each = 8.

cards.prompt: Sally has 3 brothers. Each of her brothers has 2 sisters. How many sisters does Sally have?
cards.fact: The brothers' 2 sisters are Sally plus one other girl.

cards.prompt: A brick weighs 1 kg plus half a brick. How many kilograms does a whole brick weigh?
cards.fact: If B = 1 + B/2, then B/2 = 1, so B = 2 kg.

cards.prompt: At exactly 3:15, how many degrees apart are a clock's hour and minute hands?
cards.fact: The minute hand is at 90°, but the hour hand has crept a quarter of the way to 4, to 97.5°.
